name: Cline
tagline: A coding agent available through a CLI, SDK, editor extension, and desktop app.
hook: A cloud guide to the CLI, editor extension, desktop app, automatic processes, rebuilt packages, and GUI checks.
summary: Cline's cloud-agent guide covers the CLI, editor extension, and desktop app. It says which processes start automatically, when compiled packages must be rebuilt, and which checks need a real GUI host.

techniques.title: Explain the compiled boundary before running the CLI
techniques.body: SDK exports resolve to dist rather than source. The guide warns that editing SDK code requires both rebuilding and restarting, so a stale process is not mistaken for a failed implementation.
techniques.quote:
- SDK packages (`@cline/shared|llms|agents|core|sdk`) resolve each other through compiled `dist/` (their `exports` point only at `dist/`, with no `development` source condition). You **must** run `bun run build:sdk` after changing SDK dependencies/source before running the CLI or SDK tests, otherwise imports fail with missing `@cline/*` / missing `dist/` errors. Running processes do **not** hot-reload SDK source changes — rebuild and restart.\
- Known cloud-env test artifact: `@cline/core` test `src/services/workspace/workspace-manifest.test.ts > readGitWorkspaceState > prefers origin and returns the current branch` fails because cloud VMs configure git `insteadOf` rules that rewrite GitHub remotes to `https://x-access-token:...@github.com/...`. This is an environment artifact, not a code bug.
- Some `@cline/cli` e2e assertions (`bun -F @cline/cli test:e2e`) may fail on exact tool-listing string formats; treat as pre-existing test drift, not an environment problem.

techniques.title: Separate authentication from startup health
techniques.body: The CLI launches its hub automatically, but a real agent turn still needs provider credentials. The guide describes the unauthenticated behavior and points to the CLI README for configuration.
techniques.quote: - An actual agent turn requires an **LLM provider credential**. With no credentials the default `cline` provider fails fast with an `Unauthorized` error and the interactive TUI shows a provider sign-in screen. Configure via `cline auth` or provider env vars (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLINE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`); see `apps/cli/README.md`.

techniques.title: Distinguish classes of test failures
techniques.body: The file separately labels remote rewriting in cloud VMs and CLI output-format drift. These are specific explanations of recorded failures, rather than a general instruction to ignore failing tests.
techniques.quote:
- Known cloud-env test artifact: `@cline/core` test `src/services/workspace/workspace-manifest.test.ts > readGitWorkspaceState > prefers origin and returns the current branch` fails because cloud VMs configure git `insteadOf` rules that rewrite GitHub remotes to `https://x-access-token:...@github.com/...`. This is an environment artifact, not a code bug.
- Some `@cline/cli` e2e assertions (`bun -F @cline/cli test:e2e`) may fail on exact tool-listing string formats; treat as pre-existing test drift, not an environment problem.

techniques.title: Identify which tests need an extension host
techniques.body: The extension guide distinguishes unit tests from integration and end-to-end tests that launch a real VS Code host. It lists the build and generated-code prerequisites alongside those commands.
techniques.quote:
- **Test:** `bun run test:unit` (bun-based, ~984 tests, no VS Code host needed). `bun run test:integration` (`@vscode/test-electron`, downloads a VS Code build, runs under the GUI libs) and `bun run test:e2e` (Playwright) exercise a real extension host — heavier, and the GUI libs for them are already installed.
- One-time deps (already installed, listed here in case they must be recreated): ripgrep via `bun run download-ripgrep`; VS Code test GUI libs per `CONTRIBUTING.md` (`libnss3`, `libatk*`, `libgbm1`, `xvfb`, etc.).

steal: Explain whether callers load source or compiled output.
Document missing-credential behavior separately from process startup.
Tie known test failures to specific causes and test names.
Distinguish unit checks from tests that require a GUI application.
